productionPolicy.instructionalTextRule: Keep critical instructional labels legible at mobile width; complex explanatory text belongs in HTML captions adjacent to the image.
productionPolicy.style: Photorealistic cultivation environments for observational scenes; branded scientific infographic/diagram treatment for abstract mechanisms; no decorative cannabis imagery.
productionPolicy.evidenceRule: Every visual must teach a declared objective or decision and must not imply universal legal thresholds, PPE, chemical recipes, alarm setpoints or engineering settings.
productionPolicy.accessibility: Every final visual requires concise alt text plus an expanded figure caption in the course page.

visuals.title: Cultivation hazard scan — source, pathway, consequence
visuals.teachingPurpose: Train learners to scan one realistic cultivation corridor for simultaneous slip/trip, electrical, egress, chemical and equipment-state hazards.
requiredContent: wet floor spreading toward powered equipment
damaged cord clearly visible but not sensationalized
visuals.alt: Cultivation corridor showing several workplace hazards, including irrigation water near damaged electrical equipment, a hose across the walking path, and a blocked route.

visuals.title: Hierarchy of controls for cultivation work
visuals.placement: After 'Use the hierarchy of controls — and stay inside authorization'
visuals.teachingPurpose: Show why eliminating or engineering out a hazard is generally stronger than relying only on behavior or PPE.
visuals.alt: Five-level hierarchy of controls from elimination through personal protective equipment, with a reminder that technicians only apply controls within authorization.

visuals.title: Water plus damaged electrical equipment — decision sequence
visuals.teachingPurpose: Make the stop/isolate/escalate logic visible without teaching unqualified electrical repair.
visuals.alt: Decision flow showing a technician stopping work and escalating when irrigation water approaches visibly damaged powered equipment.

visuals.title: Exposure routes and PPE function
visuals.placement: After 'Scientific foundation — match protection to the exposure route'
visuals.teachingPurpose: Connect inhalation, eye, skin and hand-to-mouth exposure pathways to appropriate categories of controls without prescribing product-specific PPE.
visuals.alt: Diagram of common workplace exposure routes—breathing, eyes, skin and hand-to-mouth—with controls matched to each route.

visuals.title: How to read a chemical label and SDS
visuals.placement: After 'Read an SDS as a structured technical document'
visuals.teachingPurpose: Teach where hazard identity, signal word, precautionary information, first aid, storage and exposure-control information live.
requiredContent: mock GHS-style label—not a real product
arrows linking task questions to sections
visuals.alt: Mock chemical label and Safety Data Sheet map highlighting where a worker finds hazard, first-aid, spill, storage and exposure-control information.

visuals.title: Restricted entry versus ordinary work scheduling
visuals.teachingPurpose: Show that a production schedule does not override a pesticide label restriction or controlled-entry boundary.
visuals.alt: Flowchart showing that a scheduled plant-moving task stops when a treated-area restriction is still active.

visuals.title: Cannabis workplace respiratory exposure pathways
visuals.teachingPurpose: Show how cultivation/processing tasks can generate plant particulate, microbial material or chemical aerosols without implying identical exposure in every facility.
requiredContent: visible conceptual particulate overlay, not exaggerated dust cloud
visuals.alt: Cultivation and processing tasks illustrating possible respiratory exposure pathways from plant particulate, microbial material and cleaning aerosols.

visuals.title: Irritant versus sensitizer — why symptoms need reporting, not self-diagnosis
visuals.teachingPurpose: Distinguish irritation from sensitization at a learner-safe level and show why repeated task-linked symptoms warrant escalation.
visuals.alt: Simplified diagram comparing irritant and sensitizer pathways that can both lead to respiratory symptoms, emphasizing reporting and professional evaluation.

visuals.title: CO₂ alarm response — senses are not a detector
visuals.placement: After 'Alarms are action signals, not diagnosis invitations'
visuals.teachingPurpose: Teach that CO₂ is colorless/odorless and that alarm response follows the site emergency plan rather than informal inspection.
requiredContent: no universal ppm alarm number shown
visuals.alt: CO2-enriched room diagram showing a fixed alarm and a worker following the emergency response rather than entering to inspect the room.

visuals.title: Pre-task safety brief — one-page visual workflow
visuals.teachingPurpose: Provide a reusable visual template linking task, hazards, controls, PPE, stop conditions, escalation and emergency communication.
visuals.alt: One-page pre-task safety brief template with fields for hazards, controls, PPE, stop conditions, escalation and emergency communication.
